problemStatement.formal: Is sum(k=1..inf) 1/2^(k^2) transcendental? More generally, for n_k with lim sup n_k/k = inf, is sum 1/2^(n_k) transcendental?
whyMatters: Gap between weak and strong growth conditions for lacunary sums

blockers: Transcendence of lacunary sums under weak growth is genuinely open
currentState.nextAction: Try to eliminate provable axioms (factorial_strong_growth, pow2_strong_growth)

knowledge.progressSummary: SURVEY: Erdos247Problem.lean has 142 lines, 0 sorries, 3 axioms. Two axioms (factorial_strong_growth, pow2_strong_growth) are provable - exponential/factorial growth dominates polynomials. The main conjecture (weak growth implies transcendence) is genuinely open.
insights: Parent file has clean infrastructure: lacunarySum, HasWeakGrowth, HasStrongGrowth, squareSeq
erdos_transcendence_strong (axiom): deep transcendence result from Erdos 1975 - not provable from Mathlib
factorial_strong_growth (axiom): PROVABLE - factorial dominates any polynomial
The open question is specifically about n_k = k^2 (quadratic growth) - between linear and superpolynomial
nextSteps: Prove factorial_strong_growth from Mathlib growth lemmas
